_comment: An EXAMPLE and shape reference for project_measures, not a shipped default: the repository's own config.json ships project_measures: {} and every report below is inert without it. Every value here is a placeholder chosen to show the shape of the setting - cast lists, chapter names, targets and thresholds are all things you replace with your own. Copy only the sections your project wants. Unrecognised keys are reported at load as config.* results, so a typo here shows up in the run rather than doing nothing quietly.

voice_separation._comment: Two channels, two casts. 'speakers' is the full prose cast used to tag quoted dialogue; 'chat_speakers' is the smaller list of names who ever post in an embedded group chat. They are separate because the chat matcher keys on lines shaped 'Name: text', which ordinary prose also produces: a prose-only name in the chat list credits messages to a character who never posts. Omit 'chat_speakers' and it falls back to 'speakers', which is right for a book with one cast.

register._comment: Chapters whose share of long words runs more than 'ratio' times the book's own median are flagged. 'exempt' excuses a chapter by file stem, with the reason recorded, for the case where the formal vocabulary is the subject matter.

exempt.12_the_hearing: the formal vocabulary is the scene: docket, affidavit, counsel

tics._comment: Repeated constructions, counted per 100,000 words against the corpus. These patterns are generic English prose habits and are a starting point; the useful ones are the phrases YOUR drafts overuse, which you find by reading your own flagged lines. 'number_words' turns on the spelled-out-number counts below.

style_report._comment: Sentence and paragraph shape targets, as [low, high] bands. The numbers below are observed across a general fiction reference corpus and are a reasonable starting point for prose fiction; set them from your own corpus if you have one. One 'sentence_bands' structure is used for both per-chapter and whole-book reporting.

check_edits._comment: Per-chapter file conventions. Every one of these is a house style choice with no default: a project that does not set them has nothing checked.

prose_check._comment: Patterns for prose that hands the reader a verdict instead of showing them the thing. These three rule shapes - stated verdicts, negation-led definition, and references to the work from inside it - are generic; the exact wording is yours to tune.

verify_citations._comment: A quotation in a character sheet is only a citation if the line also names a source file. 'citation_patterns' is how a source reference is spelled in your project.

banned_phrases._comment: Scanned from project_rules.banned_phrases in your config.json, NOT from here - this entry exists so the report is not the one configurable thing with no worked example. The shape is: {"id", "pattern", "name", "reason", "flags"}, and a hit is reported as a rule violation rather than a corpus outlier.

example_rule_for_project_rules.name: throat-clearing preamble
example_rule_for_project_rules.reason: ruled out: the sentence after it is always the real sentence

quote_length._comment: Dialogue length targets. 'peer_books' narrows the corpus comparison to named reference texts, by the source id a corpus profile lists them under, which is useful when only part of your corpus is a fair comparison. The target bands below are illustrative.
